subject: FinRepo evaluation: scout results, recommended models, and risk matrix
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finrepo.com>
Cc: Priyanka Verma <p.verma@finrepo.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinRepo evaluation: scout results, recommended models, and risk matrix

Hi Samir / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion on the content types and edge-case compliance requirements. I promised a short recap plus the initial scout results and clear next steps for an evaluation sprint. Key points below.

Summary of what we ran (attached):
- Quick benchmark: 3 representative prompt buckets (customer support, contract summarization, risk detection) run on a 1k-sample holdout you provided. Results are in benchmarks-latest.csv (attached) and a short PDF summary.
- Models evaluated (open + optimized): Llama-3-70B-q4f, Mistral-Instruct-30B-q3, Redwood-Optimized-16B-int8. We compared them vs your current on-prem baseline (FinRepo-LegalAI-v2) for accuracy, latency, hallucination rate, and cost/token.

High-level findings (quick bullets):
- Best read on intent/slot extraction: Redwood-Optimized-16B-int8 and Mistral-Instruct-30B-q3 were within 3 percentage points of FinRepo-LegalAI-v2 on intent accuracy but at ~45–60% lower inference cost.
- Hallucination: Llama-3-70B-q4f showed a slightly higher hallucination signal on contract Q&A prompts (estimated 1.5% vs baseline 0.6%). More prompt engineering reduced this but we flagged it.
- Latency: All open-model variants were within your 350ms SLO on typical inputs when served on dedicated capacity; long-context contract summarization spikes to ~1.2s on long docs.

Suggested acceptance thresholds for a parity pilot (we can adjust):
- Intent accuracy >= 94% (relative to FinRepo-LegalAI-v2)
- Entity F1 >= 0.88 on named entities important to legal/regulatory flows
- Hallucination (false fact rate) <= 0.8% for Q&A prompts
- Cost per 1k tokens <= 60% of current baseline cost for CPU/GPU profile you listed

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
1) You upload the 2k gold examples + the redaction rules to our S3 bucket by Oct 7. (I attached a sample prompt set: finrepo-prompt-set-v1.jsonl)
2) Redwood runs a 2-week A/B pilot where we serve both FinRepo-LegalAI-v2 (control) and the top open candidates behind your test harness. We produce weekly metrics dashboards.
3) Weekly syncs: Fri 11am PT starting Oct 9 to review interim metrics and any quality regressions.
4) If acceptance thresholds met, we propose a canary rollout plan and recommend quantization + KV-cache profile to match your latency/cost targets.

Open risk items we flagged for you to review:
- Regulatory: data residency for certain contract types — confirm which customer segments must remain on-prem.
- Failure modes: the Llama-3 variant had edge hallucinations on clause-references; we recommend a small guardrail layer to compare factual outputs to canonical sources for high-risk prompts.

Attachments: finrepo-prompt-set-v1.jsonl, benchmarks-latest.csv, finrepo-eval-summary-20261003.pdf

Would you like us to run an extended hallucination sweep focused on clause cross-references before the pilot?

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143
From: Samir Patel <samir@finrepo.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Verma <p.verma@finrepo.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:47:18 -0700
Subject: Re: FinRepo evaluation: scout results, recommended models, and risk matrix

Thanks Rishi — useful recap and appreciated the speed. A few clarifications from our side before we commit to uploading the full set:

1) Baseline definition: FinRepo-LegalAI-v2 is what we run in prod; it was trained on internal flagged corpora and has heavier entity post-processing. Can you ensure the A/B harness applies our post-processing layer to the open models so comparisons are apples-to-apples?

2) Hallucination threshold — 0.8% seems reasonable for high-risk Q&A. For contract summarization we need stricter guardrails: no ungrounded clause insertion; if uncertain, model should return "see source" rather than guess.

3) Residency: about 30% of our enterprise customers require EU-only processing. For the pilot we can limit the initial dataset to US accounts. We'll need a follow-up plan for EU-only.

Action items from our side:
- I'll upload the 2k gold sample and redaction rules to the S3 path you provided by COB Oct 6.
- Can you confirm the exact spec of the post-processing hook you need (format/endpoint)?

Also, curious about the cost numbers — do you have a per-hour / per-1000-token estimate for the Redwood-Optimized-16B-int8 on Dedicated vs the Mistral-30B? Even roughs will help our procurement forecast.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Engineering, FinRepo
samir@finrepo.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FinRepo evaluation: scout results, recommended models, and risk matrix

Monica/Camila — forwarding the prospect thread. Requesting quick input on two items before the pilot kickoff:

1) Post-processing hook: Samir wants us to run their entity post-processing layer on open models for fair comparison. Can we support a lightweight adaptor that posts our raw JSON to an external S3-based lambda they provide, or do we need a different approach? Tech constraints: latency budget per request is 350ms.

2) Hallucination sweep: they call out clause-insertion as high risk. I propose we run an extra targeted hallucination regression on contract Q&A with a stricter detector — threshold to flag anything that doesn't match canonical legal references. Can you confirm an ETA for the extra sweep and whether we should include Mistral-30B and Redwood-16B-int8 only, or also Llama-3-70B (given the higher hallucination signal)?

Suggested internal acceptance gating for the pilot (for your feedback):
- Gate A (safety): hallucination < 0.8% on Q&A after post-processing
- Gate B (functional): intent accuracy delta <= -1.5 percentage points vs baseline
- Gate C (cost): projected inference spend <= 65% of baseline (assuming the quantized profile)

Attachments: (none)

Thanks — if you can reply by 2pm PT I will send Samir the final pilot spec and scheduling.

Rishi
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinRepo evaluation: scout results, recommended models, and risk matrix

Rishi — quick answers:

1) Post-processing hook: we can support an S3-triggered Lambda or an HTTPS callback. HTTPS callback will add ~40–80ms depending on region; S3-lambda is similar but avoids outbound call quotas. For the pilot, recommend S3-lambda with signed artifact and a short TTL. We'll prepare a small adaptor that takes our candidate outputs and writes a pre/post csv for side-by-side scoring.

2) Halluc sweep ETA: we can run the targeted hallucination regression overnight if you limit to Redwood-Optimized-16B-int8 and Mistral-Instruct-30B-q3. If you want to include Llama-3-70B as well, add an extra 12 hours (it requires larger memory profile and more sampling). My recommendation — run the two lower-cost candidates first; if they fail Gate A then consider Llama-3 only as a conservative fallback with additional guardrails.

3) Cost estimates (very rough):
- Redwood-Optimized-16B-int8 (Dedicated, reserved profile): ~$0.29 per 1k tokens (inference only)
- Mistral-Instruct-30B-q3 (Dedicated): ~$0.42 per 1k tokens
- Llama-3-70B-q4f (Dedicated): ~$1.10 per 1k tokens
These are ballpark and will converge after we lock the quantization + KV-cache params.

I will:
- Push the adaptor spec and a sample signed S3 workflow doc to the Drive folder (link above) by EOD;
- Kick off the hallucination regression tonight limited to Redwood-16B and Mistral-30B and upload results to s3://finrepo-evals/bench-20261003/ by tomorrow morning.

If Samir confirms upload by Oct 6, we should be able to start the pilot Oct 9 as planned.

M
Monica Patel
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
